column6: Before/after table and blockade-vs-U-boat comparison are specific and sound.

Bullet 1 dated controls to "1915 and after"; Germany's War Raw Materials Department (Rathenau) began in August 1914. Reworded to "improvised after fighting began, and expanded as stalemate ... showed".

Explainer said women entered industrial work "at scale for the first time"; women were a large part of the industrial (textile) workforce long before 1914. Reworded to "entered war industries in large numbers". Note (not fixed): old q:3 keys false for "largely returned to laissez-faire", which is contested for Britain and the US, where many controls were dismantled 1919-21.
The Manifesto section "Critical-Utopian Socialism and Communism" exists and names Saint-Simon, Fourier and Owen.
Attributed "Socialism: Utopian and Scientific" to Marx; it is by Engels (1880). Now "Engels's ... Marx and Engels explicitly contrasted".

Exercise failed when worked: every limit in the Explainer (pregnancy firing, credit, marital rape) was later changed by law (PDA 1978, ECOA 1974, state marital-rape laws), so "the limits that no law touched" was an empty set. Replaced with adding customary limits such as housework.

Friedan's phrase is "the problem that has no name", not "problem with no name". Note (not fixed): calling the Equal Pay Act and Title VII "direct products of feminist organizing" overstates; both predate most second-wave organizing.

Claim "most lasting outcomes fall in the first group" fails when worked: the German zones, the Far East concessions and the UN all depended on future action yet lasted. Replaced with a prompt to note which promises in the second group were kept or broken.
Checked: Charter signed San Francisco June 1945; de Gaulle not invited, France given a zone; percentages agreement October 1944 (Romania, Bulgaria).
